messages:
maya: quick thought — if our inference model went on a coffee break, what persona would it come back as?
connor: barista bot. explains latte art using attention heads and insists on calling every request a 'special roast'. :coffee: 
liam: old librarian voice: 'Shh. Please cite your sources and reduce verbosity to maintain shelf life.'
sasha: the anti-hallucination cop. just responds with 'I don't know' and walks away. 😅
ops-bot: reminder: scheduled coffee break posted to #random at 15:00 UTC. (automated)
maya: tiny poll — react 1️⃣ 2️⃣ 3️⃣ 4️⃣: 1) Barista 2) Librarian 3) Existential roommate 4) Enthusiastic intern
connor: 1️⃣ — totally. it would give you a macchiato and a micro-batching tip.
liam: 2️⃣ — also might hand you a business-card-sized prompt template.
sasha: 4️⃣ — always offers unsolicited examples and a follow-up question.
connor: also imagine it leaves a sticky note: `TODO: lower temp from 0.9 -> 0.3`
maya: imagine the model returns as 'The Promptchef' giving recipes for few-shot examples and garnishing outputs with 🥗 examples.
liam: as your model, I recommend adding three clean examples, a system message about being concise, and a dash of negative examples.
sasha: please stop anthropomorphizing the KV cache, we're running out of persona names 😭
maya: new hack: every Friday the model gets a persona swap. name suggestions?
connor: 'Kevin the Concise' for low-latency mode.
liam: 'Evelyn the Expander' for verbose mode.
sasha: 'Ghost of Hallucinations Past' for drama.
maya: and if it comes back moody we blame a mis-set prompt. :joy: Also, anyone grabbing donuts Friday? :doughnut:
ops-bot: reminder: donut run scheduled at 10:30 on Friday. RSVP in thread.
maya: thanks y'all :heart:
